pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql; test 'AC-1' checks all existing rows are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
test 'AC-2' asserts ★ only on the starred item.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1, expects id order, starred only.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for several values incl. empty and __proto__.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits', d803bdb) deletes the 'Empty table' state test. The spec's States table row 'Empty table' (nothing, 'No items yet.', link Starred only) now has no test. The commit also leaves a stray blank line.
findings.fix: Restore the 'Empty table' test. If the owner dropped that row, record the decision and date in the spec.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. A test was deleted in the final commit, so both claims are false. The body also says test/starred.test.js covers 'each state', which is no longer true.
findings.fix: Restore the test, or correct the PR body and record the owner's decision in the spec.

lenses.note: The spec exists. The implementation matches its decisions: starred items keep their place in the list, and the view is a query parameter.
Every AC has a named test. The 'Empty table' state row lost its test in the final commit.
The tests assert behaviour. I did not run them, because the cloudflare workers pool may not be available here. One state test was deleted.
The README mentions ?show=starred. This is adequate.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is handled. The migration has a CHECK constraint. I found no defects.
The title is HTML-escaped, the SQL has no user input, and the show value is allowlisted. The route-check regex change only allows ?, and spaces and # are still refused.
The page is a bare HTML list with no styling or UI files. No browser was available.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the plain HTML in src/index.js, and there is no browser flow to run.
The title is within 72 characters, but two body claims are false (see the finding).
